headline: Finite-intensity remote fragments spread across every diffuse row give compound-Poisson+Gaussian limits; exact dense rotated {1,1,-1} output peaks converge to a value strictly below 3sqrt(2), while fixed non-Lindeberg clouds can approach 3sqrt(2) arbitrarily closely as their total intensity tends to zero.

premises.applied: For the actual R_m frame with leverage 1/m and Gram I, |phi_m(t)|<=min(1,(4pi)^(3/2)|t|^-3/2), giving an L1 envelope of 24pi and uniform density convergence.
Conditional on the compound-Poisson displacement P=p, the Gaussian quadratic-form density is <=3sqrt(2), strictly below it for p!=0 in the exact isotropic rank-three signature.

On the same explicit R_m frame, one exceptional row per bank with X=sqrt(m)Z has aggregate Gram I/m and latent aggregate OZ; hence limsup density <=3sqrt(2). This complements the new full-Gram rare-event mechanism.

new_mathematics.lindeberg: fails with positive limiting cost sum_{|a|>eps} c a^2 for every fixed nontrivial cloud

new_mathematics.near_sharp: e^{-C}3sqrt(2)<=||p_infty||inf<3sqrt(2); fixed positive C can be arbitrarily small while Lindeberg still fails

unresolved_implication: No conclusion for nonvanishing exceptional Gram/intermediate leverage with multiple interacting heavy rows, non-tight/infinite-activity diffuse aggregates lacking an independent Gaussian floor, or additional active full-matrix spectrum. The result does not prove universal sharpness of 3sqrt(2).
next_step: Attack intermediate-leverage interacting heavy rows or infinite-activity/non-tight diffuse fragmentation on an exact dense rotated core, retaining the finite-stage FBL envelope whenever applicable.
